title: Named coefficient, purity and pairing conclusions
statement:
Define the following assertion predicates on the published coefficient maps. (1) For finite-field data $D$, $\ell
e p$, finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a separated finite-type $D.k$-scheme $X$ and $m\le n$, FiniteHomComparisonConclusion conjoins etale and intrinsic evaluation compatibility, unique normalized evaluation, finite-Tor preservation of both Hom sides and comparison invertibility, both quotient cocycles and the site square; indices mean exponents $n+1,m+1$. (2) For any $D.k$-independent scheme $Y$ and $D,\ell
e p,E$, IntegralHomReductionConclusion requires a tensor presentation whose Hom is complete for complete target, and at every positive quotient a reduction presentation with invertible comparison, its evaluation equation and its Hom-transpose equation for every $K,L,T$ and arrow $T	o\operatorname{RHom}(K,L)$. (3) PurityFiniteReductionConclusion universally quantifies over finite purity settings, all $1\le m\le n$ and the original separated finite-type schemes and arrows, conjoining the eight smooth-purity, smooth trace, unit trace, composition source, composition exceptional, composition coherence, base-change and affine-orientation equations on their existing finite-Tor and smooth domains. (4) For a six-functor space morphism $f$ and compactification $c$, ProjectionCoefficientConclusion conjoins the actual projection coefficient square for positive finite quotients, integral reduction with both inputs finite Tor, integral scalar extension with target input finite Tor, and ramified finite scalar extension. (5) PerfectPairingAdjointsConclusion universally quantifies over monoidal closed categories, a strong monoidal functor, perfect pairings and their evaluation-normalized adjoint isomorphisms, comparison $c$ and second-variable arrow $r$; assuming the evaluation and pairing squares, require the dual evaluation square, adjoint and inverse-adjoint squares, the forced formula for $r$, and an isomorphism with that forward map and explicit inverse. (6) CommonStageAdjunctionDescentConclusion universally quantifies over $D,\ell,\Omega$, separated finite-type $D.k$-schemes, a separated finite-type $f$, compactification and coherent stage functors $F,G$ with specified compact-support $F$, adjunctions and transition unit/counit equations. Require a descended adjunction with exact common-stage Hom and inverse Hom representative formulas, units and counits represented at the input field, and evaluation descent for both schemes. (7) For prime $\ell$, finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, algebraic closure $\Omega$, schemes $X,Y$ with residue-field invertibility and $f:X	o Y$, BasicOperationsReductionConclusion conjoins: integral pullback and tensor preservation and good-representative finite comparisons; finite pullback/tensor invertibility, quotient and tensor-quotient equations; direct/support integral constructibility and finite reduction including transition equations; positive-level support reduction; intrinsic finite Hom evaluation and site-perfect comparison; the single predicate (2) for every $D,\ell
e p,W$; integral scalar operation comparisons and evaluation; rational pull/tensor/Hom localization formulas; the three common-stage representative predicates; unit/counit mate equations; integral, rational and common tensor associativity and unit equations; rational localization and scalar tensor equations; coherent compact-support and direct-image field actions; scalar, identity and tower laws; finite tensor associativity, unit and braiding; and finite exceptional families with uniform adjoints, quotient and scalar compatibility whenever the recorded exceptional-adjoint admissibility predicate holds. Every conditional retains its original geometry, constructibility, good-model, product, limit-triangle, perfectness and admissibility hypotheses. These definitions assert none of the predicates. The constituent notions are [def-sf-finite-hom-comparison-equations] [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models] [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons] [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] [def-pur-finite-affine-orientation-comparison] [def-sf-perfect-pairing-dual-comparison] [def-sf-common-stage-evaluation-descent] [def-sf-basic-operation-coefficient-laws] [def-sf-projection-coefficient-square] [def-fix-six-functor-datum] [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility].
